title: [Request] Single keystroke to run command without `:`
body:
Love what you've made here, this has replaced *fetch as my goto greeter. With how many times I open up salut, I'd really love to be able to map single keypresses to my pinned programs instead of having to type `:`, for instance tapping `z` to open Zellij or `n` for nvim. It's a minor optimization, but would really mean a lot to me.

I don't know C++ to implement something like this, but I've been modifying the struct at the beginning, so maybe it could be a flag somewhere in there for whether or not `:` needs to be typed?

Let me know what you think 😁
author: ygypt

comments.body:
I added the --quick-tap flag to salut. If it is used, salut will only listen for one keypress before quitting.
Note, that this means that shortcuts can also only be one letter.
This way, you do not need to press a the prefix and can start a command or close salut with one keypress.

Oh sorry lol I guess I totally glossed over that in the readme

Pardon the newbieness, how do I run this flag? It doesn't seem to do anything when passing the flag into the binary `salut --quick-tap`

For clarification I've set 4 items with 1 character binds, and with or without `salut --quick-tap` they require `:` to run. Is this a compiler flag or something I have to tweak in main.cpp?

Oh! I should have clarified, I just added the flag, it wasn't there when you opened the issue.
Running `salut --quick-tap` should skip the prefix.
Are you sure, you have gotten the latest version? You may need to pull the latest version of salut and then re-apply your changes, like for example setting binds.
I plan on creating a configuration file that would make updating salut easier.

@Wervice oh dude right on, you're awesome! That was so damn quick that I thought you were telling me the feature already existed haha

Pulled latest and it works like a charm
